messages:
sarah: heads-up — noticed a perf regression in prod after the kernel prefetch change; p99 latency for short-chat paths jumped ~30% while overall throughput stayed flat. anyone else seeing this?
raj: saw it on the dashboards, good catch. looks correlated with higher cache miss rates for prefix sets. might be fragmentation when continuous batching mixes prefixes.
kevin: pinging the profiler results I ran last night — attaching quick summary: hit_rate_pct dropped from 82 -> 65 on short sequences, median_latency_ms +12, p99_latency_ms +45. not uniform across GPU types.
anya: do we have examples of the cache keys that missed? could be our key normalization mismatch after the tokenization tweak.
kevin: yes — sample keys: `prompt_id:abc123|prefix_hash:0x7a9f|len:16` vs `prompt_id:abc123|prefix_hash:0x7a9e|len:15` — off-by-one token truncation after the new tokenizer pad.
sarah: ugh. so continuous batching is aggregating slightly different keys into same minibatch and the runtime is preferring larger kernels which evict small-prefix entries?
raj: possible. observed that kernel selector picks the fused attention kernel for mixed lengths; it increases per-batch memory churn and causes our cache eviction churn.
anya: hypothesis: mixed-length batches reduce effective prefix overlap in the KV cache because we interleave requests with nearly-matching but distinct keys, causing fragmentation. impact amplified by LRU eviction policy.
kevin: experiment idea: run a replay on canary with two changes separately: (A) prefix-preserving queueing (group by normalized-prefix-hash before batching), (B) temporary increase of cache capacity by 20% + sticky affinity to keep prefixes warm. measure hit_rate_pct & p99_latency_ms.
sarah: +1. please also record batch composition stats: percent homogeneous vs mixed-length, mean tokens per request, kernel chosen per-batch.
infra-bot: replay job queued: replay-1855123456-a (grouping), replay-1855123456-b (extra-capacity). ETA ~45m.
replay-bot: note: use trace sampling 1% and include KV-cache metrics: cache_hits, cache_misses, evicted_keys.
kevin: quick local perf experiment results (summary):
```
config: grouping=true
hit_rate_pct: 81 -> 80 (no net gain)
median_latency_ms: 120 -> 110
p99_latency_ms: 480 -> 300
notes: grouping reduced p99 but didn't fully recover hit rate; suggests eviction path + kernel selection still issue
```
anya: interesting — grouping helps tail but not hit rate. might be because grouping increases waiting time for small requests so batch window grows and triggers larger kernel path choices. tradeoff: latency vs hit rate.
raj: here's a short config snippet we tested that reduced kernel upshift for mixed batches: 
```
--batch-window-ms=8
--prefer-small-kernel-for-mixed=true
--kv-keep-ratio=0.25
```
kevin: that config lowered p99 to ~260ms but reduced throughput by ~4%. acceptable for SLOs but customers on dedicated pools might not like throughput hit.
sarah: can we try staged warmup instead of full grouping? e.g., opportunistic prefetch on tails: when a prefix enters an LRU cold state, proactively compute & store a compressed KV snapshot during low-load windows.
anya: sketch: maintain per-prefix last-used counter + cold threshold; background warmup job picks top-k cold but popular prefixes and writes reduced-size entries. tradeoff is background GPU cycles.
kevin: I prototyped a warmup worker — warmup_rate=50 prefixes/min helped hit_rate_pct +6 but memory jitter increased. full logs: hit_rate_pct 65->71, median_latency -8ms, p99 -70ms.
raj: can we combine small changes: reduce kernel upshifts, enable lightweight warmup, and keep a small grouping (only group prefixes with exact-normalized-hash match) — minimal waiting window. run A/B.
sarah: agree. action items: 1) kevin — run A/B with combined config on canary; 2) anya — produce metrics dashboard (prefix fragmentation heatmap, per-kernel eviction rate); 3) raj — add a short-term rollback plan if throughput regressions exceed 5%.
kevin: running combined A/B now, will post summary.
anya: creating dashboard tiles now, will share link in thread.
infra-bot: canary replay completed: combined-A hit_rate_pct=78, median=112ms, p99=270ms, throughput -2.1%. combined-B (no warmup) hit_rate_pct=69, p99=340ms.
sarah: looks promising. will mark for release candidate with feature flag opt-out. :thumbsup:
kevin: FYI — found one more root cause: kernel prefetch path was using raw token length instead of normalized prefix length for eviction scoring; small PR incoming to fix it.
anya: great — once PR merged we'll re-run warmup experiment to verify no memory jitter.
raj: also adding a short perf-test in CI that simulates mixed-length continuous batching to catch regressions earlier.
sarah: perfect. thanks all.
kevin: will post final numbers later tonight and close the loop.
